attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the man is the folder's own: «Οσιος Στεφανος ο Σαββαϊτης (725 - 794)», nephew of John of Damascus, born at Damascus in 725, brought into the Lavra of Saint Sabbas at ten years old. The Greek page adds two things the Romanian source did not. It gives a variant year of repose: «πέθανε ειρηνικά το 794 μ.Χ. (κατά άλλους το 807 μ.Χ.)», and the folder's `dates` already read 794 off doxologia, so no change to `dates` is proposed and the variant is recorded here. And it says his memory is repeated on 28 Οκτωβρίου, with «Για ποιόν λόγο υπάρχει διπλή μνημόνευση του Οσίου Στεφάνου, δεν γνωρίζουμε» — for what reason there is a double commemoration we do not know — guessing that today may be the translation of his relics and 28 October the memory proper. One row per church is the schema, so the row is the day page read and the second Greek day is recorded here; no second row and no second folder. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints one apolytikion, and it is taken; its text addresses him as a hierarch, «σὺ γὰρ ὡς ἱεράρχης», which neither the page's notice nor the folder makes him, and that is said in the hymn's own source line rather than acted on.

attestations.note: The day’s third entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, with its closing full stop, which is what §4 asks for and what `srbody.mjs` now hands back. **ENTRY 1 PRODUCES NOTHING AND IT IS THE FIRST ENTRY OF THIS WAVE THAT THE CORPUS HAS NO FOLDER KIND FOR.** „Св. Архангел Гаврил.“ opens „Овај велики архангел Божји празнује се 26. марта. На данашњи дан пак славе се и чествују његова јављања и чудеса кроз сву историју људскога спасења“ — this great archangel of God is celebrated on 26 March; on today’s day are celebrated and honoured his appearances and wonders through the whole history of man’s salvation. So the day is a **commemoration of apparitions**, which §4 puts with the icon feast and the relics translation and not with a person. **And there is no folder to put a row on in any case**: `ls saints | grep -i archangel` returns **nobody**, and neither does a grep for `michael-the-archangel`, `gabriel-the-archangel` or `bodiless`. Twenty-five folders carry the name Gabriel and every one of them is a man. **The corpus holds no folder for any archangel at all**, which is a reading for the author and not a gap a reader fills. The entry’s substance is reported and not written: the feast is held to have been established first on the Holy Mountain in the ninth century, under the emperors Basil and Constantine Porphyrogenitus and the patriarch Nicholas Chrysoberges, on the occasion of this archangel’s appearance in a cell near Karyes, **where he wrote the hymn to the Mother of God Достојно јест on the stone with his finger** — which is why that cell has been called the cell «Достојно» ever since; and the entry then lists the other appearances — to Moses keeping Jethro’s flock, where he told the great chosen one of God how the world was made and all else that Moses afterwards wrote in the book of Genesis; to the prophet Daniel, with the mystery of the kingdoms to come and the coming of the Saviour; to Saint Anna, with the promise of a daughter; many times to the holy Virgin while she was in the temple at Jerusalem; to Zacharias the high priest, with the news of the birth of John the Forerunner and the punishment of dumbness for not believing him; again to the holy Virgin at Nazareth with the Annunciation; to the righteous Joseph; to the shepherds by Bethlehem; **to the Lord Himself in the garden of Gethsemane, when he strengthened the Lord as a man before the passion**; and to the myrrh-bearing women. **ENTRY 2 IS A BISHOP IN GAUL AND NO FOLDER HOLDS HIM.** „Св. Јулијан еп. Кеномански у Галији.“ — Julian, bishop of Cenomanum, which is Le Mans, in Gaul. The corpus holds **twenty-five** Julian and Juliana folders and not one of them is he: `julian-companion-of-caesarius`, `julian-companion-of-euboulos`, `julian-companion-of-macarius`, `julian-companion-of-modestus`, `julian-companion-of-pamphilus`, `julian-of-africa`, `julian-of-antinoopolis`, `julian-of-emesa`, `julian-of-kandavla`, `julian-of-samosata`, `julian-of-tarsus`, `julian-of-the-brazen-gate`, `julian-of-the-dogazou`, `julian-of-the-euphrates`, `julian-presbyter-of-ancyra`, `julian-the-deacon-of-aegina`, `julian-the-martyr-18-may` and `julian-the-martyr-2-september` — not a bishop among them, not one in Gaul, and not one kept on any 13 July. Ruling 3: **reported, not created**, and the entry is substantial, which is why it is set down here in full. Some think, it says, that this saint is none other than **Simon the leper, healed by the Lord**; the apostle Peter set him bishop and sent him into pagan Gaul, where he endured great hardships but succeeded in turning many people to the faith of Christ; when he baptised the prince Defensor, many of that prince’s subjects came over to the true faith as well; by the grace of God he did great wonders, healing the sick, driving out demons and raising the dead; and he ended his life in peace, **appearing at the hour of his death, in the middle of the day, to prince Defensor at dinner**. Three of its people would be identifications and none is made: Simon the leper is a suggestion the book itself hedges with „Неки мисле“, some think; the apostle Peter is named as an ordainer, which is the same shape as Pancratius of Tauromenium on 9 July and took no row then either; and prince Defensor holds no folder. The identification is the by-name and the lavra: „Саваит“ is this folder’s own, „Подвизавао се у манастиру св. Саве Освештеног, по чему је и прозван Саваит“ is where it comes from, and the Romanian and Greek rows stand on this very 13 July. **THE TWO BOOKS DISAGREE ABOUT THE KINSHIP AND NEITHER IS PREFERRED.** This book opens „Братучед св. Јована Дамаскина“ — **cousin** of Saint John of Damascus. doxologia, off which this folder’s `birth` and `death` were both written, says «A fost nepotul nepotul Sfântului Ioan Damaschin (4 decembrie)», he was the **nephew** of Saint John of Damascus, with the doubled word the page’s own. A cousin and a nephew are not the same degree, the `related` row between the two folders already exists in both directions and carries no degree, and **nothing is changed**: both readings go into the life and the disagreement is stated as a disagreement, which is the treatment two irreconcilable books had on Cyril of Gortyna on 9 July. **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THE AGE IS THE EXACT SUBTRACTION AGAIN.** „Упокојио се у Господу 794. год. у 69. години свога живота“ — he reposed in the Lord in 794 in the 69th year of his life. 794 is the folder’s `death`, `attested` off doxologia’s «A adormit în Domnul în anul 794», and the two agree to the year. **And 794 − 69 is 725, which is to the year the `birth` the folder already holds.** That is the second time in four days that this book’s age has reproduced a birth year exactly — Anthony of the Caves on the 10 July was 1073 − 90 = 983 — and it is refused for the second time on the same ground: an age is an age, the arithmetic is the other calendar’s and not this book’s, and two numbers that agree are no more a reading than two that disagree. Nothing is written into `dates`. `types` UNTOUCHED at `venerable` and `monk`: „Преп.“ is the `venerable` and the `monk` the folder already holds is not in this heading and is not taken away by its silence. No `office`, no `locations` — the lavra of Saint Sabbas and Palestine are a narrative. No new `related` rows: the folder already relates `john-of-damascus`, `sabbas-the-sanctified` and `martyrs-of-the-lavra-of-saint-sabbas` in both directions, and the first two are the only people this entry names. **WHAT IS NEW IS ONE PHRASE AND IT IS A JUDGEMENT.** „Велики подражатељ живота св. Саве и сјајна звезда међу монасима Палестинским“ — a great imitator of the life of Saint Sabbas and a shining star among the monks of Palestine. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Îndreptătorule al Ortodoxiei, învăţătorule al dreptei cinstiri de Dumnezeu şi al curaţiei şi luminătorule al lumii, podoaba călugărilor cea de Dumnezeu insuflată Sfinte Părinte Ştefan, înţelepte, cu învăţăturile tale pe toţi i-ai luminat. Alăută duhovnicească, roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu ca să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Ștefan Savaitul», Glasul 8

english.text: Guide of Orthodoxy, teacher of true reverence towards God and of purity, and light of the world, God-inspired adornment of monks, wise father Stephen: by your teachings you enlightened all. Spiritual harp, pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Ὡς θεῖον στεφάνωμα, τὴν ἀρετὴν ἐσχηκῶς, λαμπρῶς ἐστεφάνωσας, τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν Χριστοῦ, ἐν λόγοις καὶ πράξεσι, σὺ γὰρ ὡς ἱεράρχης, καὶ σοφὸς θεηγόρος, θείων ᾀσμάτων λύρα, Πάτερ Στέφανε ὤφθης, διὸ ταὶς σαὶς φαιδρότησιν, ἠμᾶς στεφάνωσαν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος δ', Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — the only hymn on the page of «Όσιος Στέφανος ο Σαββαΐτης», and it names him. It calls him a hierarch, which the page's own notice does not; the reading is the source's and is copied as it stands

english.text: Having virtue for a divine crown, you crowned the Church of Christ splendidly in words and in deeds; for you were shown, father Stephen, a hierarch and a wise speaker of God, a lyre of divine songs. Therefore crown us too with your radiance.
